target.title: fix(clickclack): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Related: #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Assistant internal tool-trace scaffolding — `<tool_call>`-style XML blocks and `⚠️ 🛠️ … failed` tool banners, among the forms `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` strips — leaks verbatim into ClickClack chat whenever it appears in the assistant's reply text.

`sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` exists for exactly this, but ClickClack's reply never runs it: the channel's inbound turn delivers through a custom `delivery.deliver` callback (`extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.ts`) that forwards `payload.text` straight to `sendClickClackText`. ClickClack declares no durable delivery route, so the channel turn kernel always takes that custom callback and never reaches the core-outbound `sanitizeText` normalization pass. An `outbound.base.sanitizeText` hook would sit on a boundary this reply path does not cross.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the ClickClack sibling of the per-channel tool-trace fixes tracked under #90684. The other bundled chat adapters in this family (for example Twitch) reach the shared sanitizer because their inbound delivery declares a durable route, so the kernel runs the durable-first path where the core-outbound hook fires; their custom `deliver` is only a fallback. ClickClack has no durable route, so the equivalent fix has to live where its text actually leaves the process.

`sendClickClackText` is the single sender chokepoint every ClickClack delivery path funnels through — the inbound reply callback, the plain model-reply mode, the channel send adapter, and proactive outbound. Sanitizing there strips the scaffolding once for all of them and cannot be bypassed by a delivery path that skips the core hook:

```ts
const text = sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(params.text);
```

The removed `outbound.base.sanitizeText` hook would have been redundant with this and is not added.

## User Impact

ClickClack users no longer see internal tool-call XML or tool-failure banners in chat when a model leaks scaffolding into its reply text. Ordinary assistant prose is delivered unchanged. No config, schema, or API changes.

## Evidence

Real-path capture drives the production `sendClickClackText` against a local ClickClack HTTP server under `node --import tsx` and records the exact message body that reaches the wire — the same POST ClickClack's inbound `delivery.deliver` callback makes. No sanitizer, adapter, or transport code is faked; only the remote server is local. Captured against upstream `main` (before) and this PR's HEAD (after):

```
target                 input                                              before (main)                           after (this PR)
channel quote-reply    "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"       reaches wire verbatim                   "Done."
thread reply           "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"       reaches wire verbatim                   "Done."
direct message         "<tool_call>{...}</tool_call>Deploy finished."     reaches wire verbatim                   "Deploy finished."
```

Focused regression tests (`extensions/clickclack/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts`, 4 cases) assert the text handed to the HTTP client for each delivery kind (channel quote-reply, thread reply, direct message) is sanitized, and that ordinary prose is preserved. They exercise the real `sendClickClackText`; only the transport client is mocked.

Local (worktree at this PR's HEAD):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts` — 4/4
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack` — 66/66
- `oxfmt` / `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the touched file — clean
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — clean

`check:changed` lanes run on CI.
